messages.content: i am making lunch for my mother and me. she does not want cheese.
choose a lunch that leaves cheese out for your mother. what food do you have?
bread, cheese, rice, and soup. the soup has no cheese.
you could have soup with bread, or rice with soup.
my father is coming too. does that mean i should add cheese?
no. having another person at lunch does not change what your mother does not want.
we all want soup and bread. how many cups if we each have one?
three cups, one for each of you.
just the food plan, not the cups.
soup and bread, with no cheese for your mother.
did i say my father cannot have cheese?
no. you only said your mother does not want it.
i want my note to sound kind, but i am not asking for a long note.
please share what you want the note to say.
i want my brother to bring my bag back.
could you please bring my bag back?
add that i need it for school tomorrow.
could you please bring my bag back? i need it for school tomorrow.
can you make that one sentence?
could you please bring my bag back for school tomorrow?
does this say i need a new bag?
no. it asks for your bag back.
just give me the note.
could you please bring my bag back for school tomorrow?
i want to go to the park after lunch. i will ride my bike.
your plan is to ride your bike to the park after lunch.
my bike is broken. i can walk there instead.
you can walk to the park after lunch instead of riding your bike.
did that change the place?
no. you still plan to go to the park.
now i want to go before lunch, not after.
walk to the park before lunch.
what did we change first?
you changed from riding your bike to walking.
what is the plan now, in one sentence?
i will walk to the park before lunch.
help with a story about a child who cannot find a red shoe.
a child looked under the bed for a red shoe.
she finds a blue shoe there, but she is still looking for the red one.
she found a blue shoe under the bed and kept looking for the red one.
let her find the red shoe by the door.
she found the red shoe by the door and put it on.
did the blue shoe turn red?
no. there were two shoes in the story. she found the blue one first and the red one later.
where was the shoe she was looking for?
by the door.
just the color of that shoe.
red.
i cannot visit my aunt today because i am waiting for the person fixing my door.
you need to stay home for the person who is fixing your door.
she asked if i could come in the morning.
if you still need to wait then, you can tell her you cannot come in the morning.
i do need to wait all morning. write a short note.
sorry, i cannot come this morning because i am waiting for someone to fix my door.
do not say i am at work.
sorry, i cannot come this morning because i am waiting for someone to fix my door.
what reason did i give?
you are waiting for someone to fix your door.
can i say i hope to visit another day?
yes. you can add: i hope to visit another day.
what does keep mean with a book? first explain, then give one example.
it can mean to have the book instead of giving it back. an example is: you can keep this book.
does keep always mean never give it back?
no. the rest of the sentence can tell you how long. you can keep it for today does not say you can keep it for all time.
just explain the sentence about today.
you can keep it for today only says you can have it today. it does not say you can have it for all time.
now give me an example where i must return it tomorrow.
you can keep my book today, but please return it tomorrow.
which part says give it back?
please return it tomorrow.
just that part again.
please return it tomorrow.
my mother is in the kitchen and my father is in the bedroom. i am outside.
your mother and father are inside, and you are outside.
how many people are inside from what i said?
two people.
i go into the kitchen.
now three people are inside, and two are in the kitchen.
my mother goes to the bedroom.
there is one person in the kitchen and two in the bedroom. three people are still inside.
did she leave the house?
no. you only said she moved to the bedroom.
where am i now?
in the kitchen.
i chose the green shirt for today.
you chose the green shirt.
i just found my blue shirt. i like that one too.
you can choose the blue one instead if you would like it today.
i have not changed what i will put on.
then you still plan to put on the green shirt.
now i choose blue.
now you chose the blue shirt.
what was the first color i chose?
green.
and the color for today now?
blue.
i gave some apples to my brother. how many do i have left?
how many did you have, and how many did you give him?
i had eight. i gave him three.
you have five apples left.
i then gave my sister two.
you have three apples left now.
do you know if my sister ate the apples i gave her?
no. you only said you gave her two apples.
how many apples did i give away in all?
five apples: three to your brother and two to your sister.
just how many i still have.
three.
write a note as if you are my brother. say he will visit me tomorrow.
i will visit you tomorrow.
are you really coming to my house?
no. i wrote the note in your brother voice. i am not a person who can visit your house.
can you put you can write before the note?
you can write: i will visit you tomorrow.
now say he cannot come tomorrow after all.
you can write: i cannot visit tomorrow after all.
who does i mean inside that note?
your brother, because the note is in his voice.
who is helping me write it here?
picoboi is helping you write it here.
i need to ask my friend to bring the camera. i want her to know it is okay to say no.
could you please bring the camera if you can?
add that it is okay if she cannot.
could you please bring the camera if you can? it is okay if you cannot.
can you make the question shorter?
could you bring the camera? it is okay if you cannot.
keep please.
could you please bring the camera? it is okay if you cannot.
does it still let her say no?
yes. it says it is okay if she cannot bring it.
just the question, not the other sentence.
could you please bring the camera?
my friend may come tomorrow. my aunt is coming for sure.
your aunt is coming for sure. your friend may come.
my brother has not answered.
you do not know if your brother is coming.
tell me only who is coming for sure.
your aunt.
my friend just said she can come.
now your aunt and your friend are coming for sure from what you said.
should you say my brother is coming now too?
no. you have not said he answered.
just the two people we know about.
your aunt and your friend.
my story has a girl in a blue coat at the station. make the coat red instead.
a girl in a red coat was at the station.
add that she has a bag.
a girl in a red coat was at the station with a bag.
now she is at the park, not the station.
a girl in a red coat was at the park with a bag.
did the coat go back to blue?
no. the coat is still red in the new sentence.
what place changed?
the station changed to the park.
just the last sentence again.
a girl in a red coat was at the park with a bag.
i want to wash my hands, eat lunch, and go to the library. i do not have a clock time.
you can still plan the order: wash your hands, eat lunch, then go to the library.
does not knowing the time mean we do not know the order?
no. you gave the order, but you did not give a time on the clock.
which thing is after lunch?
going to the library.
i need to return a book there.
you can take the book when you go to the library after lunch.
what do i need to take?
the book you need to return.
do i return it before i wash my hands in this plan?
no. in this plan, washing your hands comes first and the library comes after lunch.
i am having a quiet morning. please do not give me a list of things to do.
okay. we can just talk for a while.
i have my tea and a book.
that can be a calm start to the day.
i do not want to talk about the book now.
okay. you do not have to talk about it.
just ask if i like the morning.
do you like your morning?
yes. thanks for keeping it simple.
you are welcome.
do not ask another question for now.
okay.
my sister had my pen. she gave it back and put it on the table.
your sister gave your pen back. it is on the table.
i cannot see it on my desk. does she still have it?
not from what you said. she put it on the table, not on your desk.
i found it there.
you found the pen on the table.
now i put it in my bag.
your pen is in your bag now.
who had it before i got it back?
your sister.
where should i look for it now?
in your bag.
write why i could not go to school yesterday.
what was the reason you could not go?
the bus left before i got to the station, and i had no other way to get there.
i could not go to school yesterday because the bus left before i got to the station and i had no other way to get there.
make it shorter, but do not say i felt tired.
the bus left before i got to the station, and i had no other way to get to school yesterday.
why did you not say i felt tired?
you did not say you felt tired. you asked me not to add that.
what was the reason from what i said?
the bus left before you got to the station, and you had no other way to get there.
can you just give me that as a note?
the bus left before i got to the station, and i had no other way to get to school yesterday.
i want six books on my shelf. i have two there now.
you have two books there and want six.
how many more would i need to make six?
four more books.
i add one book.
now you have three books there and need three more to make six.
if i want six, does that mean i already have six?
no. six is how many you want. you said you have three there now.
i take the last book back off the shelf.
now there are two books on the shelf again.
how many more to have six now?
four more books.
in the note i will bring your bag, who is your?
your bag is the bag of the person you are writing to.
i am writing it to my sister.
then it is the bag of your sister.
and who will bring it?
you will, because you are the person saying i in the note.
now write it from my sister to me.
i will bring your bag.
the words look the same. did the people change?
yes. now your sister is saying i, and your bag is the bag that you have.
just tell me who brings it in the new note.
your sister.
i want a quiet place to read with good light. my bedroom is quiet but has little light.
is there another place that is quiet and has light?
the living room has no one in it, and the sun comes in there.
the living room could give you what you want: quiet and light.
the kitchen has light too, but people are cooking.
the kitchen may not be as quiet. the living room still gives both things you asked for.
do not choose a place just because it has light.
right. you asked for both quiet and light.
which place did i say has both?
the living room.
what was wrong with the bedroom for this plan?
you said it has little light, so it does not give you the light you want.
picoboi, why ask me a question instead of making up what i mean?
if i do not understand, asking can help me give an answer about what you really want.
what if i ask where my bag is and you have no idea?
i should say i do not know, then ask where you last had it if you want help looking.
what if i already said it is by the door?
then i should use what you said and answer that it is by the door.
so you should not ask the same thing again if i said it already?
right. i should use what you already said when i can.
can you still give a wrong answer?
yes. i am a small model and can get things wrong.
just your name now.
picoboi.
write a short story where a boy cannot find his book but then finds it.
a boy could not find his book on the table. he said it was lost, but then he looked in his bag and found it there.
do not say someone took it.
a boy could not find his book on the table. he looked in his bag and found it there.
what did he think at first?
he said the book was lost.
what did he know after looking?
the book was in his bag.
did he find it on the table in this story?
no. he found it in his bag.
just the last sentence of the short story.
he looked in his bag and found it there.
i have a red bike, a green bag, and a blue coat. answer only what i ask.
okay.
what color is my bag?
green.
now just say the thing that is blue.
your coat.
do not tell me the color of each thing again.
okay.
which thing is red?
your bike.
how many things did i first tell you about?
three things.
i want to visit my friend, but i can only stay for a short while.
you can tell your friend before the visit that you can only stay a short while.
she asked if i can have dinner there.
can you have dinner there and still leave when you need to?
no. i need to go home before dinner.
you can say you would like to visit but need to leave before dinner.
write that in a kind way.
i would like to visit, but i need to go home before dinner.
she said an afternoon visit is fine.
then you can visit in the afternoon and still go home before dinner.
what did i ask you to remember about when i have to go?
you need to go home before dinner and cannot stay long.
i want a nice note for my mother for a holiday, but do not say which holiday.
i hope you have a nice day. thank you for all you do for me.
can it thank her too?
i hope you have a nice day. thank you for all you do for me.
do not say which holiday it is.
i hope you have a nice day. thank you for all you do for me.
which holiday did i tell you it was?
you only said it is a holiday. you did not say which one.
can you make it one sentence with thank you?
thank you for all you do for me, and i hope you have a nice day.
just that sentence again.
thank you for all you do for me, and i hope you have a nice day.
a girl had a book to use for a while and gave it back. did she lose it?
not from that sentence. it says she gave the book back.
she said she could not find it for a while before giving it back.
she could not find it for a while, but then she gave it back.
if she gave it back, does she still have it?
no. she gave the book back.
can you write one simple sentence about the end?
the girl found the book and gave it back.
do we know who gave it to her to use?
no. you have not said who gave it to her to use.
do not make up that person.
okay. we can leave that part out.
my brother and i both want rice for lunch.
you both want rice for lunch.
i now want soup instead, but he still would like rice.
you want soup, and your brother still would like rice.
does changing what i want change what he would like too?
no. you only changed what you want.
i have both ready to eat.
you can each have the food you want.
just tell me what to put on my plate.
soup.
and what should he have?
rice.
write my friend is coming tomorrow as a question.
is my friend coming tomorrow?
does that still say she is coming for sure?
no. it asks if she is coming. it does not say it is sure.
now write it so it says she is coming, not as a question.
my friend is coming tomorrow.
make it about this evening instead.
my friend is coming this evening.
did you leave it as a sentence saying she is coming this time?
yes. the new sentence says she is coming this evening.
just the sentence.
my friend is coming this evening.
i wrote my uncle will come, but i only think he might. what should i change?
you could write: my uncle might come.
is might the same as will?
no. might is a way to say you are not sure.
i want to tell my mother, but i do not want to say i am sure.
my uncle might come, but i do not know for sure.
now he said he cannot come.
then you can tell your mother: my uncle cannot come.
which sentence is right for what we know now?
my uncle cannot come.
did he say yes at any point in our talk?
no. you were not sure if he could come, then said he cannot.
i found my book and put it in my bag. now i need my coat.
your book is ready in your bag. you can look for your coat next.
my mother asked me to bring her cup to the kitchen first.
you can take her cup to the kitchen, then look for your coat.
does that mean i need to find the book again?
no. you already put the book in your bag.
i took the cup to the kitchen. what is next?
look for your coat.
it is on the chair. i have it now.
now you have your book in the bag and your coat with you.
what did i do between finding the book and getting the coat?
you took your mother cup to the kitchen.
